threat_event: Ransomware at the PMS vendor takes the PMS offline for several days: no profiles, e-prescriptions, EPCS, claims, or PDMP reporting, and patient data may be stolen from the vendor
threat_source: Cybercriminal ransomware group attacking the PMS vendor
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single SaaS dependency for every pharmacy function; vendor RTO (12 hours) longer than the BIA RTO (4 hours); no paper downtime kit, printed medication lists, or contact list; no cyber insurance
likelihood_basis: EV-005 (one PMS for every function); EV-037 (vendor RTO 12 hours); EV-030 (no downtime kit or contact list); EV-020 (no cyber policy payment)
existing_controls: Vendor SOC 2 controls and backups; BAA
treatment_plan: Adopt the P08 runbook; build the paper downtime kit (weekly printed active-patient medication list, label template, paper logs); written transfer arrangement with a nearby pharmacy; ask the insurance agent about cyber coverage

threat_event: Ransomware or a remote attacker enters the counter desktop through the vendor's remote-support agent or a phishing email, encrypts it, and steals scanned prescriptions, reports, the mailing-list export, and the CSOS key
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Remote-support agent allowed unattended access until 2026-08-06; shared automatic sign-in account with administrator rights; desktop on the same network as customer Wi-Fi; no security training
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-03 desktop; SYS-01 sessions; CSOS certificate
likelihood_basis: EV-004 (unattended remote access); EV-014 (shared administrator account); EV-016 (one network); EV-031 (no security training); EV-AC-17 (9 unwatched vendor sessions, P07 test 2026-08-06)
existing_controls: Built-in antivirus; automatic updates; agent switched to attended mode 2026-08-06
treatment_plan: Keep the agent in attended mode and log each session; own standard desktop accounts; desktop encryption; guest network; annual training

threat_event: The relief pharmacist dispenses under the owner's PMS account, so dispensing and controlled substance records name the wrong pharmacist and no one can tell who did what
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Only one pharmacy account in the PMS; password kept on a card in the counter drawer until 2026-08-06
likelihood_basis: EV-001 (one pharmacy account); EV-021 (owner's account signed in on relief days); EV-017 (password card in the drawer); EV-IA-2 (2 of 10 records name the owner, P07 test 2026-08-06)
treatment_plan: Create the relief pharmacist's own PMS account with the pharmacist role before the next relief shift; owner keeps the administrator role for settings only

threat_event: A customer device or a nearby attacker on the store Wi-Fi attacks the desktop or the camera recorder
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One network for the desktop, camera recorder, and customer Wi-Fi; Wi-Fi password printed at the counter
likelihood_basis: EV-016 (desktop, camera recorder and customer phones on one network); EV-017 (Wi-Fi password at the counter); EV-SC-7 (P07 network scan 2026-08-06)
existing_controls: Router firewall; host firewall; SaaS traffic uses TLS
treatment_plan: IT consultant sets up a separate guest network and a separate network for the camera recorder; new Wi-Fi password not posted

threat_event: Burglary aimed at the controlled substance stock takes the unencrypted counter desktop, exposing scanned prescriptions, controlled substance reports, and a mailing-list export of about 2,100 patients
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No full-disk encryption on the desktop; local files kept indefinitely; pharmacies are burglary targets for drugs
likelihood_basis: EV-014 (no encryption; patient files on the desktop); EV-017 (controlled substance stock in the same store); EV-035 (risk walk-through)
existing_controls: Monitored alarm; camera; locked controlled substance cabinet
treatment_plan: Turn on built-in full-disk encryption; delete the mailing-list export and any report older than needed; keep the recovery key in the sealed envelope

threat_event: The email and file suite vendor holds faxed prescriptions and compounding records with no BAA in effect (impermissible disclosure; contract terms the pharmacy did not accept)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: BAA offered in the admin console but never accepted; fax-to-email sends every faxed prescription to the inbox
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-02 email and files; SYS-06 fax
likelihood_basis: EV-012 (BAA not accepted; faxed prescriptions in the inbox); EV-013 (fax-to-email delivery)
treatment_plan: Accept the vendor's BAA in the admin console and confirm it covers email and file storage; keep a copy in the BAA folder

threat_event: Someone at the counter uses the open PMS session or the store administrator password while the owner is at the compounding bench
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Desktop never locks; PMS administrator signs in with a password only inside the store
likelihood_basis: EV-014 (screen lock off); EV-017 (open PMS session; screen faces the counter); EV-002 (password only in the store)
existing_controls: Prescription department closed to the public
treatment_plan: 3-minute desktop lock with PIN; MFA for the administrator role at every location; position the screen away from the counter

threat_event: Altered or fraudulent controlled substance prescription records go unnoticed, and the one-business-day DEA report is missed
threat_source: Insider or external attacker; vendor staff
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Daily EPCS audit report never read before 2026-08-06; no procedure for 21 CFR 1311.215(c); EPCS certification finding never checked before first use
likelihood_basis: EV-003 (daily EPCS reports unopened); EV-030 (no reporting procedure); EV-005 (no certification report on file); EV-AU-6 (first review, P07 test 2026-08-06)
existing_controls: PMS analyzes the audit trail daily (inherited); certification report on file since 2026-08-05
treatment_plan: Read the EPCS report each business morning and log it; written decision steps and contacts for the one-business-day report (P08); recheck the certification each time it is renewed

threat_event: Patient details pasted into a consumer AI chatbot with no BAA are kept or used for training by the vendor
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Free personal account; no BAA; training setting on; no AI rule
likelihood_basis: EV-032 (free account; training setting on; patient details per the owner); EV-033 (no BAA on the free plan); EV-019 (no BAA on file)
treatment_plan: No PHI in any AI tool without a BAA (POL-01 9.5); turn off training; delete history; four-factor breach risk assessment for the 6 conversations with counsel (P10)

threat_event: A compounding calculation or formulation taken from the AI chatbot is wrong and the error reaches a patient
threat_source: AI tool error relied on by the pharmacist
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Chatbot used to check compounding calculations; no rule requiring an independent check against a reference or the master formulation record
likelihood_basis: EV-032 (calculation checks in the history); EV-030 (no AI use rule found)
treatment_plan: Stop using any AI tool for calculations or formulations; every calculation checked against the master formulation record and a standard reference; second calculation on paper for high-risk compounds

threat_event: The pharmacist-owner is suddenly unavailable or loses the only phone, so nobody can run the PMS as administrator, order Schedule II stock, or reach vendors
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One person holds every role, credential, and the CSOS key; second factor on one phone; no coverage arrangement
likelihood_basis: EV-002 (one second-factor device); EV-025 (one CSOS certificate holder); EV-028 (no employees); EV-034 (BIA worksheet)
existing_controls: Relief pharmacist available about 2 days a month
treatment_plan: Relief pharmacist's own account; decide on a CSOS power of attorney; sealed recovery codes and emergency access sheet with the owner's attorney; transfer arrangement with a nearby pharmacy

threat_event: Someone other than the owner signs a Schedule II order with the CSOS key on the shared desktop
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: CSOS private key in the browser store of the shared automatic sign-in account
likelihood_basis: EV-014 (CSOS key in the shared account); EV-023 (order confirmations to the owner's email)
existing_controls: Key protected by its own password; wholesaler order confirmations go to the owner's email
treatment_plan: Move the key to the owner's own desktop account; report any loss or compromise to the certificate authority within 24 hours (21 CFR 1311.30(e))

threat_event: A security incident is not recognized, or a notice deadline is missed (HIPAA, Florida, DEA one business day, PDMP, CSOS 24 hours)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No incident plan, contact list, or training; several short clocks unknown to the owner
likelihood_basis: EV-030 (no incident plan or contact list); EV-031 (no security training); EV-036 (DEA and CSOS clocks not known)
treatment_plan: Adopt the P08 runbook and notification matrix; print the contact list; walk through the runbook with the relief pharmacist and the IT consultant

threat_event: OCR or DEA enforcement after a complaint, breach, or inspection, because no risk analysis or written policies existed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No risk analysis or written security policies before 2026-09-04
likelihood_basis: EV-030 (no risk analysis or written policies found)
treatment_plan: Keep this register current; review every August and after major changes; keep documents 6 years; operate the HICP small-practice measures to build a recognized security practices record

threat_event: Hurricane or a long power outage closes the store for several days
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single store; refrigerated stock; desktop and paper records on site
likelihood_basis: EV-026 (Florida storefront); EV-017 (desktop and paper records on site)
existing_controls: PMS is cloud-hosted and reachable from the laptop over a phone hotspot; Florida law allows up to a 30-day emergency supply of essential maintenance medications other than Schedule II in areas under a declared state of emergency (Fla. Stat. 465.0275(2))
treatment_plan: Accepted: residual risk Low. Take the laptop and the CSOS key home when a hurricane watch is issued; print the active-patient medication list
